text:
I moved my side project's database to a 2 GB VPS and figured Postgres would be fine. It's known for being solid, and I didn't have much data. But memory goes fast if you keep the defaults and let the app open as many connections as it likes.

Following the standard advice, I gave shared_buffers 512 MB, which is a quarter of the RAM. That part was fine. The trouble was that the app was allowed up to 200 client connections, and every backend process takes its own chunk of memory on top of that. The server had almost nothing to spare, and the kernel responded accordingly: the OOM killer fired three times in the first month, and each time it killed Postgres.

I didn't fix it with some obscure config setting. I put pgbouncer in front of the database, which dropped the connection count from 200 to 20, and the app never knew the difference.

Below I'll go through what broke, what I changed, and what I'll check next time before putting Postgres on a small server.
